name: Tobramycin (ophthalmic)
reviewed_by: William Gregory M. Rivero, MD, FPCP, DPSN
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero
summary: All tobramycin products registered in the Philippines are 0.3% eye drops or eye ointment. The ophthalmic label gives the same dose for everyone and no kidney adjustment. Injectable tobramycin, an aminoglycoside that needs kidney dosing and level monitoring, is not registered in the Philippine list and is not covered here.

monitoring: Clinical response of the eye infection; hypersensitivity. The label notes nephrotoxicity and ototoxicity with systemic aminoglycosides, not with eye use.

pediatric.approved_ages: Safe and effective in children (label indications); not established under 2 months (label 8.4).

sources.citation: Novartis Pharmaceuticals Corporation. (2026). TOBREX (tobramycin ophthalmic ointment) 0.3% [Prescribing information; US FDA-approved label, NDA050555, set ID 5b66bba3-cf97-4a9c-b618-ba5f277f20f6, version effective October 26, 2026]. DailyMed, U.S. National Library of Medicine.

adult: JUDGMENT: all tiles green ('no adjustment') because the product is ophthalmic and the label gives one dose for everyone. Alternative: hide the strip. 'Low systemic absorption' is not stated in this label, so it is not claimed.
Selected label is the ointment; PH products are mostly 0.3% solution (drops) plus ointment.
If an injectable tobramycin is registered later, it needs its own aminoglycoside record (serum creatinine/CrCl dosing, TDM).
